title: Μυῖα
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 238. Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« »). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Μυῖα ἐμπεσοῦσα εἰς χύτραν κρέως, ἐπειδὴ ὑπὸ τοῦ ζωμοῦ ἀποπνίγεσθαι ἔμελλεν, ἔφη πρὸς ἑαυτήν· « Ἀλλ’ ἔγωγε καὶ βέβρωκα καὶ πέπωκα καὶ λέλουμαι· κἂν ἀποθάνω, οὐδέν μοι μέλει. »
sentences.tr: Muia empesousa eis chytran kreōs, epeidē hypo tou zōmou apopnigesthai emellen, ephē pros heautēn· « All’ egōge kai bebrōka kai pepōka kai leloumai· kan apothanō, ouden moi melei. »
sentences.l: A fly, having fallen into a pot of meat, when she was about to be choked by the broth, said to herself: « Well, I for my part have both eaten and drunk and bathed; and even if I die, it is nothing to me. »
sentences.n: The three perfects — βέβρωκα (ἐσθίω), πέπωκα (πίνω), λέλουμαι (λούω) — put her whole life behind her as a thing completed: what is done is done and cannot be taken back. Eating, drinking and bathing together make up the round of a comfortable day, so the list is a whole good life in three words, and the broth she is drowning in has served her as all three. κἄν is καὶ ἐάν run together by crasis, with the subjunctive ἀποθάνω: 'even if I die'. μέλει is impersonal with the dative of the person concerned, οὐδέν an adverbial accusative — 'it is no concern of mine at all'.

sentences.t: Ὁ λόγος δηλοῖ ὅτι ῥᾴδιον φέρουσι τὸν θάνατον οἱ ἄνθρωποι, ὅταν ἀβασανίστως παρακολουθήσῃ.
sentences.tr: Ho logos dēloi hoti rhāidion pherousi ton thanaton hoi anthrōpoi, hotan abasanistōs parakolouthēsēi.
sentences.l: The story shows that men bear death easily, whenever it comes on without torment.
sentences.n: βάσανος is the touchstone that tests gold and then the rack that tests a man, so ἀβασανίστως is 'without being put to the question' — death arriving with no pain to try the dying. παρακολουθέω is to follow close at someone's heels, which makes death an attendant rather than an assault. ὅταν with the subjunctive states what holds as a rule, not what happened once.
